verdicts.h1_news_sentence: For news coverage, attention rose 0.07 standard deviations for each standard deviation the official measure worsened (95% interval 0.02 to 0.10, 21 city and category pairs, about 206 independent pair-years). That is a weak link, and the interval excludes zero, so H1 is supported for news coverage.
verdicts.h2_news_sentence: For news coverage, the reaction to worsening and to improving could not be told apart. The slope was 0.05 when the problem worsened and 0.10 when it improved. The difference was -0.05 (95% interval -0.14 to 0.11). The interval includes zero, so H2 is not supported for news coverage.
verdicts.h3_news_sentence: For news coverage, Safety showed the largest gap in 1 of 3 cities. Hong Kong: Safety ranked 1 of 7 (70% of periods moved in opposite directions; the largest was Safety at 70%). New York City: Safety ranked 4 of 8 (45% of periods moved in opposite directions; the largest was Education at 67%). London: Safety ranked 6 of 6 (34% of periods moved in opposite directions; the largest was Housing at 59%). H3 predicted the largest gap in at least two cities, so it is not supported.
verdicts.h1_search_sentence: For search interest, attention rose 0.26 standard deviations for each standard deviation the official measure worsened (95% interval 0.19 to 0.42, 18 city and category pairs, about 336 independent pair-years). That is a weak link, and the interval excludes zero, so H1 is supported for search interest.
verdicts.h2_search_sentence: For search interest, the reaction to worsening and to improving could not be told apart. The slope was 0.37 when the problem worsened and 0.17 when it improved. The difference was 0.20 (95% interval -0.10 to 0.47). The interval includes zero, so H2 is not supported for search interest.
verdicts.h3_search_sentence: For search interest, Safety showed the largest gap in 0 of 3 cities. Hong Kong: Safety could not be tested. New York City: Safety ranked 4 of 7 (41% of periods moved in opposite directions; the largest was Environment at 47%). London: Safety ranked 4 of 6 (41% of periods moved in opposite directions; the largest was Environment at 52%). H3 predicted the largest gap in at least two cities, so it is not supported.
